record.title: Unitree releases UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 Base checkpoint and fine-tuning code
record.summary: Unitree's official UnifoLM-WLA repository records a September 28 release of the WLA-1.0 Base checkpoint and fine-tuning code. The current official model repository lists a 12.5 GB safetensors checkpoint under Apache-2.0, while the official guide describes a local episode evaluation path. These artifacts make part of the earlier open-release promise inspectable; they do not establish the reported 64-task performance or broad physical generalization.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Unitree's official repository lists the WLA-1.0 Base checkpoint and fine-tuning code as released on September 28, 2026.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The official model repository lists a 12.5 GB safetensors checkpoint with an Apache-2.0 license, and the official guide describes a local episode evaluation path.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Unitree reports a 6B policy trained on about 2,500 hours and spanning 64 real-robot tasks.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent task-level physical outcomes for the released checkpoint and evidence across the claimed 64 tasks remain unavailable in this review.
The listed dataset collections and reported task count were not audited for complete coverage, overlap or held-out evaluation.

brief.importance_rationale: If a released 6B whole-body policy materially supports cross-task humanoid manipulation, an inspectable checkpoint and fine-tuning path could broaden research access and enable controlled follow-up; the score reflects that consequence while the breadth/performance claim remains vendor-reported.
limitations: No code was downloaded or executed; no independent physical evaluation was performed.
No full per-task success table, trial protocol, dataset completeness audit or cross-end-effector reproduction was completed.
The current evaluation guide notes the model server supports Dex1, not WBT; artifact release does not establish broad deployment coverage.

The current official model repository lists a 12.5 GB safetensors checkpoint under Apache-2.0, while the official guide describes a local episode evaluation path. These artifacts make part of the earlier open-release promise inspectable; they do not establish the reported 64-task performance or broad physical generalization.

technical.claimed_result: Unitree describes WLA-1.0 as a 6B policy trained on roughly 2,500 hours and spanning 64 real-robot tasks. The official source does not provide a complete independently validated task-level outcome table in the reviewed materials.
technical.compute_or_cost: Official guide describes a local evaluation workflow and a 24 GB GPU requirement for the documented setup; actual inference latency and energy were not measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official repository records the September 28, 2026 checkpoint and fine-tuning-code release. The linked official model repository currently lists safetensors files totaling about 12.5 GB and an Apache-2.0 license; the official guide documents a local episode evaluation path.
technical.implementation_status: Checkpoint and fine-tuning code are listed by official Unitree surfaces. No code was executed and no checkpoint was downloaded in this review.
technical.mechanism: The release provides the UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 Base checkpoint and fine-tuning code for a vision-language-action humanoid policy.
technical.novelty: The newly inspectable checkpoint and fine-tuning surface partially resolves the earlier code/weights-unavailable state.
technical.regime: Publicly listed base checkpoint and fine-tuning code for Unitree's humanoid robotics policy; physical task performance remains bounded by the publisher's evaluation materials.
technical.reproducibility: Artifacts improve inspectability, but task-level protocols, dataset completeness and independent physical reproduction remain unresolved.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched baseline was assessed in this artifact-release review.

brief.title: Unitree releases UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 Base checkpoint and fine-tuning code
brief.why_it_matters: A public base checkpoint and fine-tuning path let researchers inspect and begin testing a humanoid whole-body manipulation policy, changing the release state from a project-page announcement to a reproducible artifact surface. The important open question is whether the reported breadth survives task-level controlled evaluation and independent physical reproduction.
